chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Snub Mosely's USO show through Army camps
summary: Smith toured Army camps from Seattle to Maine with Snub Mosely's six-piece band behind a show of dancers, singers and comedians.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah. Either '39 or '40. Because in '41 I went out on the road with Snub Mosely when the war broke out. See, it was '41 when the war broke out, and Snub Mosely was on the road with a USO show.
Did you go all over the country?
Yeah, we went everywhere, except Texas and Louisiana. I think we missed Louisiana.... Mississippi we may have... We were mostly in Illinois... We stayed up in that territory.

No. We didn't make Mississippi. We jumped all the way to Seattle, Washington, and played all the way back through Oregon, Utah, Colorado, and I think we made Kansas... I think we missed Missouri and made Kansas, and we played Iowa, and then we come on up through Michigan...yeah...and ended up way up yonder in Bangor, Maine, and come back down, and went down to Maryland, and that's when we closed it. ( ?)Orlando Robeson(?) was with us on that show.
And the band at this stage consisted of you and Snub...
No. Let me see. Who was playing tenor? Sedric, I believe, was the tenor player.

No, we didn't have Joe Keyes. I think we had Ed Rome. Yeah, Ed Rome. He had a brother who played trumpet with another band -- I forget what band that was. Anyway, I think that's who I think was on trumpet, Ed Rome. Because Coatner(?), he couldn't go. He had to stay there. He was playing trumpet.
And was it only Army camps that you play?
No. Mostly to give a show. Because had a show... There were 14 of us altogether, but it wasn't but six in the band. There were 8 people in the show with...

Yeah, they had dancers and singers, and then two comedians... John Mason and Johnny Vaggard(?) was two comedians. They did the comedy work. I can't think of this boy's name -- him and this girl did the dancing. Then they had two or three other little acts.
